# dsh-image-tiler
English | 简体中文

> Upload a screenshot, a photographed document, or a long comic page and the model reads the small
>
text in it. Without this plugin it does not: one request image carries at most 1024 vision tokens,

> so the harness rescales anything larger before the model sees it, and an 8000x8000 screenshot
> ar

rives as a ~1300px-wide picture with the text already gone.
>
> This is **not** an official DeepSeek
product and does not imply DeepSeek endorsement.
## What it does
The plugin replaces the attachment store's admission step. When a prompt carries an image too large

to survive the harness' own downscaling, it cuts the image into adjacent regions and submits each
re

gion as its own image, in the same message. Every region is then transmitted at its own
resolution,

so the model sees the source at the resolution it was uploaded at instead of at the
resolution one i

ees the source at the resolution it was uploaded at instead of at the
resolution one image can hold.
Measured on a real boot (DSH 0.2.0-rc.2, desktop host, an 8000x8000 PNG of small text):
| | as one image | tiled (default settings) |

| what the model receives | 2048x2048, re-encoded | 20 regions of 2000x1600, one per image part |
|

glyph height in the image | 10 px in the source, unreadable after scaling | 10 px, unchanged |
| tex

t rows the model can resolve | 0 | 8 |
| contrast in the text band | 11.2 | 29.7 |

Small images are not touched, and neither are images the provider would only trim a little: the
plug

in cuts a picture up only when the print it replaces would have been about seventy percent of the
so

urce's own size or less. An ordinary 1920x1080 screenshot is printed at 1708x960 — eleven percent
na

rrower, which no one can see — so it stays whole and leaves the message's image budget to pictures
t

h no one can see — so it stays whole and leaves the message's image budget to pictures
that need it.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0` (declared in `engines.dsh`, and as `peerDependencies` on
`@

deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment` / `-attachment-local`; verified against `0.2.0-rc.2`). The range
covers

the whole `0.2.x` line, prereleases included, so a harness patch or rc bump does not
disable the plu

gin.
- Node.js 20 or newer (the host's own requirement).
- Status: **experimental**. The tiling poli

cy is verified, but the plugin replaces a core service,
so treat a version bump of the harness as a

reason to re-check it.
- `sharp` is bundled as a dependency. The plugin ships no prebuilt binaries o

f its own; pnpm
installs `sharp`'s platform package for your machine as usual.
## Security posture

- No telemetry, no network access, no credentials handling, no background service.
- No `prepare`, `

install`, or `postinstall` scripts; the package contains JavaScript, YAML, and text.
- No child proc

esses. Nothing is spawned or executed; `sharp` runs in-process through its native
binding.
- Images

are decoded and re-encoded in memory. Tiles are written by the harness' own attachment
store, to the

same place the original image would have gone, and nothing is written anywhere else.
- The only fil
es the plugin reads are the ones the store hands it.
## How it works

1. `apply(ctx, config)` mounts `TilingAttachmentStore` under the `attachments` service name, so it
r

eplaces the official `attachment-local` store while extending it. Storage, admission limits,
normali

zation, and reads all stay the base implementation's.
2. `admitPromptContent(content)` is the single

call the session controller makes before it appends a
user message. The override plans a tile layou

t for each image part, crops the source with
`sharp`, and returns the tiles as image parts.
3. Becau

se the replacement happens before admission, the tiled images become part of the stored
session mess

age itself. Replay, resume, and fork rebuild exactly what the model originally saw.
4. The layout co

mes from `lib/geometry.js`, which transcribes the provider's own image projection
(patch/downsample

grid, 1024-token budget) and picks the grid whose regions land closest to 1:1
with what the provider

would otherwise have sent. A layout has to buy back at least twice the
detail per source pixel befo

re it is worth the image parts it spends, so a source the provider
would print at nearly its own siz

e yields exactly one tile.
5. The whole batch is checked against the store's own limits before admis

sion — piece count, each
piece's stored size, and the total. If it does not fit, or if any tile woul

d be a sliver, the
original image is sent instead and the reason is logged. A plugin that tiled badl

y must never
cost the user their picture, and the store refuses a whole message over one oversized m

never
cost the user their picture, and the store refuses a whole message over one oversized member.
## Known limitations
- **A tiled upload costs more vision tokens than a single image.** Cutting one source into N pieces

sends N images; that is the point, but a 20-tile upload is a much larger request than a 1-image
uplo

ad.
- **Tile size is capped by the store's normalization policy.** A tile larger than
`normalizedIma

geMaxPixels` (4194304, i.e. about 2048x2048) is downscaled after the crop, which is
why the planner

fills the whole `maxImagesPerMessage` budget (20 by default) instead of using a
few big pieces.
- **

The piece count follows `maxImagesPerMessage`, so a lower value gives worse tiles.** With the
budget

lowered to 6, an 8000x8000 source becomes five 4579x915 strips: complete and clear, but not
the sha

pe a reader would pick. The default of `20` produces the squarest layout.
- **Several large uploads

in one message share the budget.** Ten images at once leave two pieces
each, below the four a layout

needs to divide a source rather than shave it, so they are sent at
the provider's print. Send large

images one or two at a time when their detail matters.
- **Tiles are whole regions, not overlapping

pages.** A glyph on a seam is cut in half, and neither
neighbouring tile shows it whole.
- **Only t

he inline image path is tiled.** Files attached as documents, and images that arrive
through other t

ools, are not.
- The plugin was verified against `0.2.0-rc.2` on Windows. Other platforms are untest

s, are not.
- The plugin was verified against `0.2.0-rc.2` on Windows. Other platforms are untested.
